topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the scope, learning objectives, and clinical relevance of the lecture series on cancer biology.

topics.label: Carcinogenesis as a disruption of cellular genetics and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core biological concepts of cancer as a progressive failure of cellular differentiation, genetic regulation, and tissue architecture, along with the models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the clinical and histological characteristics of tumour invasion, metastatic dissemination, and the stepwise progression from benign lesions to invasive malignancies.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumours by tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the direct and systemic mechanisms by which primary tumours and metastatic lesions cause clinical disease and death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence across human tissues and multicellular species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distribution and frequency of different tumour types in human populations and across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the rationale for early cancer detection, the histological basis of successful cervical screening, and the limitations of screening for other tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and giving reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
